WCAG Audit

Check any digital asset for accessibility against WCAG 2.2 AA.
SKILL · RUNS AUTOMATICALLY WHEN IT APPLIES

What it does

Audits a digital asset against the WCAG 2.2 Level AA accessibility standard and produces a severity-ranked findings report, with verifiable evidence behind every Pass and every Fail. It reports problems; it does not modify the asset.

What it can audit

  • Live web pages and URLs (rendered in a real browser)
  • Static HTML and CSS files
  • PDF documents (tagging, reading order, alt text, headings, tables)
  • Word (.docx) documents and PowerPoint (.pptx) decks

When to use it

Any time something needs an accessibility check before it goes out - a public web page, a customer-facing PDF, a training deck, a marketing doc. It also powers the Accessibility dimension of The Test Master, which calls it automatically during a web audit.

How to trigger it

"check this for WCAG 2.2 AA"

"run an accessibility audit on this page"

"is this PDF accessible for screen readers"

"does this deck meet ADA / Section 508"

The one rule to remember

A clean automated scan is never proof of conformance. Automated tools catch at most about 57% of accessibility issues, so the skill reports "no automated violations detected; manual review still required" rather than "WCAG conformant." A real conformance claim needs human and screen-reader testing.

Requirements

What this skill needs in order to run. Added 2026-08-20.

Skills - None.

Connectors / MCP servers - None.

Folder access - Read access to the page, PDF, Word document or deck under audit, and write access to the report destination.

KB modules / context files - None.

Repos - None.

If something is missing - An unreadable target is LOUD. The defining SILENT rule: a clean automated scan can never be reported as WCAG AA conformant, because automation covers only part of the criteria - reporting conformance from a passing scan is the failure this skill is built to prevent. Report what was checked and what still needs a human.
